title: Middlebrook Truss Bridge reconsidered and procurement policy updated
subtitle: Heritage demolition on East Mill Street, Operations Centre rezoning, salary grid, land acknowledgement, tenders and toll booths
overview: Council reopened its earlier decision on the Middlebrook Truss Bridge. It rescinded the plan to remove the bridge without replacement {{vote:m19}}. It then directed staff to consult the Township of Woolwich and a community group to investigate new options {{vote:m20}}.

Council endorsed a new Procurement Policy, amended so the Mayor and Clerk keep signing authority for contracts of $2 million and over {{vote:m6}}. It approved a revised Land Acknowledgement {{vote:m5}}. It also approved demolition work at heritage-listed properties on East Mill Street in Elora, keeping the original stone structure at number 19 {{vote:m7}}.

On planning, Council approved the official plan and zoning changes for the future Municipal Operations Centre and nearby industrial lands in Fergus {{vote:m8}}. It also approved a rezoning at 77 McQueen Boulevard {{vote:m10}} and a part lot control exemption {{vote:m9}}. After a closed session, Council reported approving a 2023 draft salary grid and directed staff to prepare an implementation plan within the 2024 budget {{vote:m3}}. Council also awarded a digital sign retrofit and a compact tractor tender, and approved three September toll booth fundraisers.

decisions.detail: Council rescinded its 2022 decision to remove the bridge without replacement and directed staff to work with Woolwich on removing the superstructure while keeping the abutments and centre pier {{vote:m19}}.
Council directed staff to consult the Township of Woolwich and the Save Middlebrook Bridge Community Group to investigate new options {{vote:m20}}.
Council endorsed the policy with an amendment keeping the Mayor and Clerk as signing authority for contracts of $2 million and over, and enacted it by by-law immediately {{vote:m6}}.
Council approved full demolition of 19A and removal from the heritage register, and partial demolition at 19, leaving the original stone structure on the register {{vote:m7}}.

decisions.item: Operations Centre land and industrial designation
decisions.detail: Council approved an official plan amendment and zoning amendments for lands on Gartshore Street and Gregson Court, Fergus, supporting a Municipal Operations Centre and future industrial use {{vote:m8}}.
Council approved the 2023 draft salary grid and consultant-recommended pay practices, with an implementation plan to come within the 2024 budget {{vote:m3}}.
Council approved rezoning application RZ03/23 and found no further public consultation was required {{vote:m10}}.
Council approved the revised Land Acknowledgement following additional feedback from First Nations {{vote:m5}}.
